hints.title: Virtual Array Fisher-Yates Sampling
hints.text: Treat the matrix as a flattened sequence of cells and map flipped coordinates to available tail positions without initializing full grids.

hints.title: Sparse Index Remapping Map
hints.text: Pick a random index between zero and remaining count minus one. Swap chosen value with the element at remaining count using a sparse dictionary.

hints.title: Flip and Reset Blueprint
hints.text: In flip(): pick r = randint(0, total - 1). actual = map.get(r, r). total -= 1. map[r] = map.get(total, total). return [actual // n, actual % n]. In reset(): map.clear(), total = m * n.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import random

class Solution:
    def __init__(self, m: int, n: int):
        self.m = m
        self.n = n
        self.total = m * n
        self.mapping = {}

    def flip(self) -> list[int]:
        r = random.randint(0, self.total - 1)
        self.total -= 1
        actual = self.mapping.get(r, r)
        self.mapping[r] = self.mapping.get(self.total, self.total)
        return [actual // self.n, actual % self.n]

    def reset(self) -> None:
        self.mapping.clear()
        self.total = self.m * self.n
```

variables: K: number of flip operations performed
complexity.notes: Constant time flip and reset using sparse hash map swapping.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Maintaining an explicit m x n grid requires up to 10^8 elements, exhausting memory constraints.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sparse hash table stores only flipped indices up to K entries.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of Fisher-Yates sampling adapted with sparse coordinate mapping.
